From: security-ops@verdanthealth.com
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-30T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Request: service isolation architecture + CAIQ/SIG tie-out

Hi Rafael,

We're preparing Verdant Health's vendor risk package and need a concise package describing Redwood's service isolation model for Dedicated and Private deployments. Specifically we need:

- A high-level network diagram showing control plane / data plane separation and egress controls (PNG/PDF preferred)
- A short narrative (1 page) describing how tenant isolation is enforced across Dedicated pools and Private VPC installs
- A CAIQ/SSP mapping highlighting where our SIG/CAIQ controls are answered by architecture (spreadsheet preferred)
- Evidence artifacts (topology images, example firewall rules, KMS boundary statement) as a single bundle if possible

Can you confirm what you can provide and an estimated delivery date? Verdant is aiming to submit this to their procurement team by 12/09.

Thanks,
Jordan Lee
Security Ops, Verdant Health
security-ops@verdanthealth.com

P.S. Their third-party assessor is BrightShield (audits@brightshield.com) and may ask follow-ups once they review the packet.

Rafael —

Attached are the first-pass artifacts: a draw.io-internal diagram (redwood_service_isolation_diagram_v1.drawio) and an exported PDF. Notes:

- The diagram shows three logical tiers: Edge (ingress LB + TLS termination), Serving Fabric (Dedicated pools + Private VPC workers), and Control Plane (management plane run in a separate VPC with strict egress rules).
- Tenant KV caching and model runtime instances live in the Serving Fabric; control-plane APIs sit behind a management plane with no public data-plane access.
- Egress controls: per-tenant NAT / subnet ACLs for Private installs; dedicated SNAT pools + egress proxy for Hosted/Dedicated.
- KMS boundary: customer-managed keys supported for Private installs (HSM/KMS integration shown); Hosted uses Redwood KMS with customer key wrap for enterprise customers.

Question for Verdant: do they require network-level diagrams showing specific cloud regions/subnets (we currently provide logical diagrams plus a region-specific appendix on request)?

I'll finish the annotated callouts tonight and can hand off the CAIQ mapping to Marissa. Link to working folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cRedwoodVerdantEvidence

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Security Architect, Redwood Inference

Jordan / BrightShield team —

Attached is the assembled evidence dossier we've prepared for Verdant Health:

Attachments (bundle): evidence-bundle-verdant-20261202.zip
Contents (high level):
- 1-page control summary: "redwood_control_summary_verdant.pdf"
- Network diagrams: "redwood_service_isolation_diagram_v1.pdf" (logical) and drawio source
- CAIQ mapping spreadsheet: "redwood_caiq_mapping_v2.xlsx" (cells call out document/artifact names)
- SIG CSV extract: "sig-responses-verdant.csv" (selected control responses)
- Supporting artifacts: NAT rule excerpt, KMS boundary statement, management-plane runbook excerpt

High-level takeaways for Verdant:
- Tenant isolation is enforced at multiple layers: network (per-tenant subnets / NAT), runtime boundary (container/GPU pool isolation + process-level cgroups), and key management (customer keys for Private installs).
- Control plane is logically separated and cannot directly access tenant model state: management APIs authenticate via mTLS and are audited; data-plane traffic is restricted by egress proxies.

Next steps: please review the bundle and let us know any follow-ups BrightShield needs. We can produce region-specific subnet diagrams if Verdant requires them for their procurement packet.

Delivery ETA note: We can provide any additional redacted firewall/NACL examples or an ops walkthrough MTR (30–45 minutes) if BrightShield prefers a short call.

Best regards,
Rafael Mendes
Head of Security Partnerships
Redwood Inference
